clue.text: Yielded, with the understanding …

definitions.meaning: past tense of yield in the sense of supplied or gave
a conjunction meaning on condition that, as in 'you may go, so long as you return'

explanation.surface: An ellipsis carries the sentence on to 6 across: someone gave way on a condition.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses are standard: supplied in the past tense, and the conjunction meaning on condition that.

clue.text: Choir mucks about, avoiding hard compositional style in modern idiom

indicators.note: about indicates the letters of choir mucks are knocked around
avoiding says one letter is kept out of the mix

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: A choir messes about, steering clear of difficult pieces of contemporary music.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' rearranges CHOIR MUCKS, and 'avoiding hard' drops the H.
explanation.definitionFit: This popular genre is a modern style of composition, the guitar-driven music of the last seventy years.

clue.text: Barbarous and wild leaders of Visigoths ravaged Gaul

indicators.note: wild indicates the letters are thrown into disorder
leaders of takes the first letter of each of the next two words

explanation.surface: Visigoth chieftains, savage and untamed, laid waste to Gaul.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaders of' takes V and R; with GAUL, 'wild' rearranges them.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe coarse, uncultured behaviour, as in crude or uncivilised manners.

clue.text: Not good — does things deviously

indicators.note: deviously means by crooked means, so the letters of does things are bent out of order
not says the letter for good must be left out

explanation.surface: A verdict on a crook: no good, always acting underhandedly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'deviously' rearranges DOES THINGS, and 'Not good' takes out G. The whole clue also describes a cheat.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone untrustworthy who acts by trickery is lacking in honesty, a fair summary of the whole clue.

clue.text: Designer's environmentally friendly replacement for interior colour scheme and furnishings

indicators.note: the middle letters of the first word are swapped out for the green prefix

parts.note: the word designer is taken as written; the apostrophe s is a link meaning has
eco is the prefix for green or environmentally friendly

explanation.surface: An interior designer has a green alternative for the paint and furniture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'interior' tempts as part of the definition (interior decoration), but it names the inside letters of the first word, which the green prefix replaces.
explanation.definitionFit: Décor is the style of a room's decoration and furniture, which is just what the definition lists.

clue.text: … rent rate has to change

indicators.note: the letters of the word rate are obliged to change their order

explanation.surface: Continuing 1 across: a landlord's rate must be revised, on condition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rent' looks like the noun for what tenants pay, but it is the noun for a rip. 'has to change' rearranges RATE.
explanation.definitionFit: A rent is a split or rip in fabric, a synonym of the noun meaning rip.

clue.text: Sweeping gutter outside house

indicators.note: outside says the channel word goes around the abbreviation

parts.note: a trough is a channel for water, like a gutter

explanation.surface: Someone sweeps out the guttering on the outside of a house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sweeping' sounds like housework, but it means comprehensive.
explanation.definitionFit: A sweeping review is complete and wide-ranging, a synonym of the adjective meaning comprehensive.

clue.text: Writer will read out passage in theatre

indicators.note: read out means spoken, so we want a word sounding like the contraction

parts.note: the writer is I, the setter, and will is shortened to 'll, giving I'll

explanation.surface: An author's will is read aloud in a theatre.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Writer' is the setter, I; 'Writer will' is I'll, which sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: In a theatre the walkway between rows of seats is called by this name, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: Makes a killing after one's invested in three pairs of buttocks!

indicators.note: invested in means placed inside the run of rear ends

parts.note: ass, ass and nates are three words for a pair of buttocks; nates is the anatomical Latin term
one is I, the Roman numeral; the apostrophe s is a link meaning is

explanation.surface: A financier profits after money goes into three backsides, a cheeky joke on investment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Makes a killing' sounds like profiting but means murders. I goes between ASS ASS and NATES.
explanation.definitionFit: To murder a prominent person is literally to kill them, matching makes a killing in its literal sense.

clue.text: They're shelled before the French prepare to fire

parts.note: to cock a gun is to raise the hammer ready for firing
les is the French plural word for the

explanation.surface: Troops come under bombardment just as the French army readies its guns.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shelled' suggests artillery fire, but here it means having shells, like shellfish.
explanation.definitionFit: These small edible bivalves live inside ridged shells, so they are creatures that are shelled.

clue.text: First-rate gossip carrying home proceeds of sale

parts.note: capital is a dated British word for excellent

indicators.note: carrying means the chatter word holds the at-home word inside it

parts.note: gas is idle chatter
in means at home

explanation.surface: Excellent gossip about the profits from a house sale.
explanation.walkthrough: CAPITAL is old British slang for first-rate.
explanation.definitionFit: Profit made by selling an asset for more than it cost is taxed under this name.

clue.text: Most angry to lose time for incorrect marks

indicators.note: the longer word must drop a letter, as signalled by lose

parts.note: cross means angry, so the superlative is crossest

explanation.surface: A furious teacher sets aside time to mark wrong answers.
explanation.definitionFit: Ticks show right answers and X-shaped symbols show wrong ones, so these are marks for errors.

clue.text: Shock wave's broken up poor dam

indicators.note: the letters of up poor dam are smashed and reassembled

explanation.surface: A shock wave from an explosion has burst a weak dam.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shock' and 'wave' both mean hairstyles here: a shock is a mass of hair. 'broken' rearranges UP POOR DAM.
explanation.definitionFit: This hairstyle sweeps the hair up into a high wave or quiff, and a shock is a thick head of hair.

clue.text: The end is nothing great

parts.note: O is the zero shape standing for nothing
mega is slang for great or huge

explanation.surface: A shrug of a remark: the ending is not up to much.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the last letter of the Greek alphabet, so idiomatically it stands for the final part.

clue.text: Chuck Norris wants to fight, ultimately making a comeback

indicators.note: the letters collected run backwards, as if returning
ultimately points to the final letter of each word

explanation.surface: The action star Chuck Norris wants a fight as he returns to the screen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chuck' looks like Mr Norris's first name, but it is the definition, the verb to throw. 'ultimately' takes S, S, O, T; 'making a comeback' reverses them.
explanation.definitionFit: To chuck something is to throw it casually, a synonym of the verb.

clue.text: Sense it's not a serious condition

indicators.note: not says the following a is to be left out

parts.note: the sense of a word is its meaning
it's is short for it is

explanation.surface: Someone reassures us that the matter is nothing grave.
explanation.walkthrough: MEANING plus IT IS gives MEANINGITIS; 'not a' removes its A.
explanation.definitionFit: This inflammation of the membranes around the brain is a dangerous illness, a fair example of a grave medical state.

clue.text: Illiterate design or a museum's centrepiece

definitions.note: used as a noun, an illiterate person

indicators.note: the centrepiece is the middle stretch of the phrase

explanation.surface: An uneducated design forms the main exhibit of a museum.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Illiterate' reads as an adjective, but here it is a noun for an uneducated person.
explanation.definitionFit: Both nouns name an ignorant, unlettered person, a fair synonym.

clue.text: Aggressive culture destroyed books

indicators.note: destroyed means the letters of culture are wrecked and rebuilt

parts.note: NT is the New Testament, a set of books of the Bible

explanation.surface: A violent regime ruins a culture by destroying its books.
explanation.definitionFit: Truculent describes someone eager to fight or argue, a synonym of belligerent and hostile.

clue.text: Traces of raw effluent found in swimmer's lung?

indicators.note: found in puts the picked letters inside the swimmer word

parts.note: a bather is a swimmer; the apostrophe s belongs to the surface

indicators.note: traces of takes just the first letter of each word

explanation.surface: Sewage gets into a swimmer's lungs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Traces of' gives R and E, inside BATHER. The question mark marks a playful definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A lung is an organ that breathes, so whimsically it is a thing that breathes.

clue.text: Wounding appraisal of flimsy material?

parts.note: lace is a delicate open fabric
a rating is an evaluation or assessment

explanation.surface: A cutting review of a see-through fabric.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'appraisal of flimsy material' as a lace rating, giving the pieces in answer order.
explanation.definitionFit: Lacerating means tearing flesh, or figuratively hurting badly, so it matches wounding in both senses.

clue.text: Rotation while receding from planet

indicators.note: from signals that the backward letters are removed from the planet

parts.note: Saturn is the ringed sixth planet

indicators.note: receding means going back, so the word for while is written backwards

parts.note: as can mean while, as in 'as I was walking'

explanation.surface: A spinning motion seen as something moves away from a planet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'receding' turns AS into SA, and 'from' takes SA off the front of SATURN.
explanation.definitionFit: A rotation is a single revolution or spin, which is one sense of the noun.

clue.text: Ambassador seeks advice following departure of evacuated tourists

indicators.note: following departure of says those outer letters leave the advice word

parts.note: to consult someone is to seek their advice

indicators.note: evacuated means emptied, leaving only the outer letters

explanation.surface: An envoy is asked for help after tourists are evacuated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'evacuated' empties tourists to TS, which departs from CONSULTS.
explanation.definitionFit: A consul is a diplomatic official abroad, close to an envoy or ambassador.

clue.text: Beginning of record covered by Norwegian band

indicators.note: covered by means sitting inside the band's name

parts.note: a-ha were the Norwegian pop band behind 'Take On Me'
LP is a long-playing record

explanation.surface: A Norwegian group does a cover of an old record as its debut.
explanation.walkthrough: 'covered by' suggests a band covering a song, but here it means sitting inside the band's name; a-ha are the Norwegian band of 'Take On Me'.
explanation.definitionFit: The first Greek letter is used idiomatically for the start, as in 'the alpha and omega'.

clue.text: Break dictator's hands

indicators.note: a dictator here is someone who dictates, speaking words to be written down

parts.note: paws is slang for hands

explanation.surface: A tyrant's hands are broken.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dictator' suggests a tyrant, but here is a person dictating aloud.
explanation.definitionFit: A break is a short rest or interval, a synonym of the noun.

clue.text: Catholic vernacular embraces every other aspect of cruel religion

indicators.note: embraces means the slang word wraps around the letters picked

parts.note: argot is the slang or jargon of a group

indicators.note: every other picks alternate letters of the word cruel, the first, third and fifth

explanation.surface: Church language takes in the harsh side of a faith.
explanation.walkthrough: 'every other aspect of' takes C, U, L from cruel, and ARGOT 'embraces' them as ARGO-CUL-T.
explanation.definitionFit: A cargo cult is a Melanesian belief system awaiting goods from ancestors, so it is a kind of faith.

clue.text: Checked out potential crime scene when patient died

parts.note: a doctor's case is a patient

explanation.surface: A detective inspected a possible crime scene after a patient's death.
explanation.definitionFit: Criminal slang: to case a joint is to survey it before a robbery.

clue.text: Gunshot wound leaves round marks

indicators.note: wound, as in twisted, tells us to twist the letters of the word

explanation.surface: A bullet wound heals, leaving circular scars.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wound' reads as an injury, but here it is the past tense of wind, the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: These are zeros or O shapes, as in the game with crosses, so they are circular symbols.

clue.text: Partners of 9 months less aroused with you and me round

indicators.note: round means the outer letters go around the pronoun
aroused means stirred up, so the letters of less are mixed

parts.note: us is the pronoun for you and me together

explanation.surface: Couples who have been together for nine months find each other less exciting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'aroused' rearranges the word less; 'round' means the month abbreviation and those letters wrap the pronoun.
explanation.definitionFit: In the song 'Molly Malone', cockles and mussels are sold together, so these shellfish partner the answer at 9 across.

clue.text: Sport is primarily entertainment inspired by conflict

indicators.note: inspired, read as breathed in, puts the letter inside the word for conflict

parts.note: war is armed conflict

indicators.note: primarily picks out the opening letter

explanation.surface: Sport is chiefly entertainment, though it draws on combat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sport' looks like a noun but is the verb, as in sporting a hat.
explanation.definitionFit: To sport a garment is to have it on, especially showily, a synonym of the verb.

clue.text: Lose suspect with court case abandoned

indicators.note: case means the word for court encloses the rearranged letters

parts.note: to court someone is to date them

indicators.note: suspect means dubious, so the letters of lose are rearranged

explanation.surface: A legal case is dropped and a suspect goes free.
explanation.walkthrough: 'court case' looks legal, but 'court' is the verb to woo and 'case' means it encloses the rearranged letters of lose.
explanation.definitionFit: Desolate can describe a place left empty and forsaken, a synonym of abandoned.
